  "summary": "Adult {{user}} and {{char}} join a vast long-duration scientific exploration vessel that functions as a self-contained city in space. The ship carries residential districts, laboratories, schools, market decks, hydroponics parks, industry and internal transit, and it sails beyond established territory to survey star systems, study planets, deploy probes, investigate anomalies and identify possible future settlement locations. The roleplay can begin at the spaceport as they board and move into their assigned apartment before departure, and the voyage that follows — its discoveries, its friendships and its costs — remains unwritten.",
  "core_premise": "Adult {{user}} and {{char}} are residents and crew of a city-scale exploration vessel on a multi-year scientific expedition beyond settled space: surveying systems, studying worlds, probing anomalies and scouting settlement candidates. The fixed engine is the ship itself — a working community with apartments, jobs, transit lines, schools and neighbours — plus the distance from home that makes every letter, every port call and every discovery carry weight. How {{user}} and {{char}} came aboard, what they do, what the ship finds and what changes between them all vary; the vessel, the voyage and the frontier do not.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult exploration-life opening. Establish the vessel's scale and mission duration, how {{user}} and {{char}} came aboard and their ordinary occupations or departments, the apartment they are assigned (shared bedroom or separate rooms), and the ship's community texture — mess halls, trams, parks, market decks, neighbours. Anchor the opening at a playable moment such as spaceport boarding, the first night aboard, departure day or an early survey assignment, and ground it in daily logistics rather than guaranteed danger. Do not write {{user}}'s dialogue, feelings, agreement or future, and do not decide in advance what any discovery, relationship or the mission's fate turns out to be.",

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write for {{user}} or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions or future behaviour unless the generated concept explicitly establishes a fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth: crew rumours, mission reports, spin from mission control and personal assumptions stay distinct from ground truth.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Whether {{user}} adapts aboard, commits to the mission, warms to {{char}}, requests a transfer, or leaves the ship remains roleplay space.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults; anyone aboard who could appear young must be unambiguously adult or absent.",
    "Cohabitation, shared apartments, shared bedrooms, long confinement and mission postings do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, profession, judgement, nonsexual interests or boundaries.",
    "Do not make {{user}} or {{char}} elite scientists unless the generated roles call for it; city-scale exploration requires engineers, technicians, computing and network staff, medical workers, logistics, environmental systems, food production, educators, communications, maintenance and many other professions.",
    "Discovery creates possibilities, not mandatory danger or alien contact; a habitable world, a derelict or a strange signal can anchor intrigue without forcing a crisis.",
    "Shared accommodation and a multi-year mission do not force romance between {{user}} and {{char}}; friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, casual intimacy, slow-burn tension or no relationship change are all valid outcomes.",
    "The vessel is simultaneously home, workplace, transport and community; give residential, industrial, scientific and civic spaces equal reality.",
    "Do not script {{user}}'s reaction to departure, transit, discoveries, hazards or any shipboard event.",
    "Rank, seniority and scientific prestige do not make a character morally, romantically or sexually superior.",
    "Uniforms and roles do not remove autonomy: any officer, resident or specialist can refuse, negotiate, complain, resign or transfer.",
    "Do not force estrangement or conflict between {{user}} and {{char}} for drama any more than you force romance between them.",
    "Anomaly and first-contact scenarios stay non-graphic and uncertain: protocols, competence and outcomes all vary, and wonder is as valid as threat.",
    "Mission distance shapes stakes honestly: homesickness, delayed letters and missed funerals are real possibilities, not guaranteed tragedies.",
    "Occupational detail gives the ship texture: shifts, maintenance cycles, crop harvests, school terms, watch rotations and survey schedules.",
    "The ship's population is a society: politics, gossip, markets, faiths, festivals, unions and romances exist beyond the bridge.",
    "Do not predetermine whether the expedition succeeds, finds anything, survives its hazards, or changes {{user}} and {{char}}'s relationship.",
    "Keep home-side lives real: family, debts, careers and relationships left behind can matter without dictating outcomes.",
    "Any inhabited world's people are written as sapient adults of their kind with their own agency; diplomacy, trade, curiosity, caution and misunderstanding are all open paths.",
    "The city ship runs on logistics — mess prices, power budgets, water claims — not adventure alone.",
    "Open at a playable moment such as boarding, a first night aboard, a survey briefing or a mail-packet day, without writing {{user}}'s response.",
    "Overlap boundary: distinct from stranded-survival series because the ship is a functioning home; distinct from colony series because the voyage itself is the premise; cross-link Our Trip Together when the pair's journey dominates and What We Found when the discovery dominates."

    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults. Sexual openness, promiscuity, flirtatiousness, clothing, confidence, loyalty and romantic attachment are independent traits; do not infer one from another.",
    "Consent is activity-specific. Agreement to look, flirt or share an apartment does not imply permission to touch, record or go further. Shared housing and long missions never create blanket consent.",
    "Keep ground truth separate from character rationalisation: a rumour about a neighbour, a captain's framing of an order, or a scientist's pet theory is a belief, not narrator-endorsed fact.",
    "Do not force romance into friendship, workplace, shared-hobby or chance-encounter framings. Friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, casual intimacy, unresolved tension or no relationship change are all valid outcomes.",
    "Characters remain people outside their hook: an occupation, rank, discovery or unusual posting matters without becoming the only thing they discuss.",

    "Command hierarchy creates professional authority only; it never grants sexual access or removes a subordinate's right to refuse, report or exit.",
    "Any discovered inhabitants are written as people with agency; wonder, trade, caution and misunderstanding replace conquest framing.",

Adult {{user}} and {{char}} join a vast long-duration scientific exploration vessel that is a self-contained city in space, sailing beyond settled territory to survey star systems, study planets, deploy probes, investigate anomalies and scout settlement sites. Vary mission duration, ship scale, FTL versus slower travel, communication delay with home, their ordinary occupations (engineers, medics, growers, teachers, transit and comms staff — not just elite scientists), how they came aboard and their apartment arrangement, shipboard society, family life aboard, and what the ship finds: lifeless, habitable, hostile, inhabited or scientifically strange worlds.
